course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Digital Literacy
course.description: Digital Literacy is designed to equip students with essential digital skills needed for academic success and modern workplace performance. The course focuses on four key areas: Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft PowerPoint, and Digital Productivity Tools. Students learn to create professional documents, analyze and visualize data, design effective presentations, and use digital platforms to collaborate, communicate, and work more efficiently. Through hands-on activities, students apply formatting and document-structuring techniques in Word; perform data calculations, cleaning, and charting in Excel; design clear presentation slides in PowerPoint; and use tools such as Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Canva, and ChatGPT to support academic tasks and creative work. By the end of the course, students will be able to produce well-formatted reports, interpret datasets through basic analytics, deliver presentations using professional visual design principles, and utilize modern digital tools for problem-solving and collaboration in academic and real-world settings.

clos.description: To formulate professional documents using Microsoft Word. LLO 1.1: To apply formatting, page layout, and document structuring tools to produce clean and readable documents. LLO 1.2: To insert and format tables, images, styles, and headers/footers to build multi-page reports. LLO 1.3: To use advanced features, e.g., track changes, citations, and table of contents to produce academic reports.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Inquiry-based learning Lab-based learning Problem-based learning
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Lab 1: Process to use Word Problem 1: Develop Word Midterm Exam

clos.description: To formulate excel file by visualizing data using Microsoft Excel. LLO 2.1: To use formulas and functions (SUM, AVERAGE, MIN/MAX, references) to calculate & summarize data. LLO 2.2: To clean, sort, filter, and validate datasets for accurate data analysis. LLO 2.3: To create charts and apply basic logic functions (IF, conditional formatting) to interpret and present data.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Inquiry-based learning Lab-based learning Problem-based learning
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Lab 2: Process to use Excel Problem 2: Develop Excel Midterm Exam

clos.description: To formulate effective presentations using PowerPoint. LLO 3.1: To apply design principles (layout, color, typography) to create visually clear slides. LLO 3.2: To use images, icons, SmartArt, and charts to communicate ideas effectively. LLO 3.3: To deliver short presentations using professional slide transitions, animations, and speaking techniques.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Inquiry-based learning Lab-based learning Problem-based learning
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Lab 3: Process to use PPT Problem 3: Develop PPT Final Exam

clos.description: To demonstrate modern digital tools for collaboration, communication, and content creation. LLO 4.1: To use Google Workspace/Microsoft 365 tools to collaborate, share files, and manage cloud storage. LLO 4.2: To create digital forms, surveys, and Canva designs for academic or event purposes. LLO 4.3: To use AI (ChatGPT) to enhance productivity while maintaining ethics.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Inquiry-based learning Lab-based learning Problem-based learning
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Lab 4: Google Workspace Lab 5: Microsoft Form Lab 6: Canva Lab 7: ChatGPT Final Exam

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Students are responsible for understanding how to use resources responsibly. Not knowing the rules, misunderstanding the rules, running out of time, submitting “the wrong draft,” or being overwhelmed with multiple demands are not acceptable excuses. There are no excuses for failure to uphold academic integrity. Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Form a study group and take full advantage of such an opportunity to share the understanding with classmates. Thoughtful participation in class discussions, thorough preparations for the class, and consistently well-developed responses to the assignments are expected. Students are expected to explain lessons to each other and have self-study from the other source. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned Submit assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Course policy Policy for Description Attendance Students Must attend class on-site and on-time (Three lates is counted as a one-time absence). Must do self-study and read the relevant documents in the Internet/library. Academic Integrity & Collaboration Students Must complete assigned tasks (assignments, quizzes, and exams) only by himself/herself. Questions might be asked during/after submission Must join class activities actively Must work independently on the midterm and final exam. Should discuss course material with other students Must feel guilty if they: (1) present work of others as their own, and (2) give unauthorized assistance to other students. Homework Students Must complete and submit assignment tasks on time. Must proper justifying quotations from appropriate and authorized resources. Must use APA style for in-text citation and reference list. Penalties Students Can absent (Absent + Permission) at most 5 times per course; otherwise, they will need to repeat the same course in the following year. Get one absent if they get three late (Students are considered as late, when they join class after 5 min start) Will be accused of plagiarism, if they (1) present work of others as their own, and (2) give unauthorized assistance to other, and get scored Zero. Will be deducted score if they submit classwork or homework late Will be reported to the Study Office, and handled in accordance with the university regulations if they violate the university code of conducts Note: If you are unclear whether a particular situation may violate the university code of conducts, you should ask the instructor.
